# useRovingTabIndex

> WAI-ARIA roving tabindex: one Tab stop per widget, arrow keys/Home/End inside, disabled items skipped.

🟡 intermediate · React 19.0+ · Custom Hooks › Accessibility & interaction · support: universal

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-roving-tab-index`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-roving-tab-index)

## Concept

Gives the active item `tabIndex=0` and every other item `-1`, so the widget is a single Tab stop. `getItemProps(index)` adds a ref, `onKeyDown` (arrows by orientation, Home/End, optional wrap, RTL) and `onFocus` (clicking an item makes it active).

## Problem

A toolbar of ten buttons costs keyboard users ten Tab presses to get past it. Composite widgets (toolbars, tab lists, listboxes, menus, grids) are expected to be one stop with arrow-key navigation inside.

## When to use

- Toolbars, tab lists, radio-like button groups, listboxes and menus built from buttons.
- Selection-follows-focus tabs (use `onActiveChange` to select).

## When not to use

- Native `<input type="radio">` groups and `<select>` — the browser already provides arrow-key behaviour.
- Widgets where focus should stay on a container/input and items are referenced with `aria-activedescendant` (comboboxes).
- Full grid/tree widgets — use a library such as React Aria, which also handles typeahead and 2-D navigation.

## API

```ts
function useRovingTabIndex(options: {
  count: number;
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' | 'both';
  loop?: boolean;
  initialIndex?: number;
  isDisabled?: (index: number) => boolean;
  dir?: 'ltr' | 'rtl';
  onActiveChange?: (index: number) => void;
}): {
  activeIndex: number;
  setActiveIndex: (index: number, options?: { focus?: boolean }) => void;
  getItemProps: (index: number) => RovingItemProps;
};
```

| Parameter                     | Type                                   | Description                          |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `count`                       | `number`                               | Number of items.                     |
| `orientation` _(optional)_    | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical' \| 'both'` | Default `horizontal`.                |
| `loop` _(optional)_           | `boolean`                              | Wrap at the ends. Default `true`.    |
| `isDisabled` _(optional)_     | `(index) => boolean`                   | Skipped by arrows, Home and End.     |
| `dir` _(optional)_            | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'`                       | Swaps Left/Right in RTL layouts.     |
| `onActiveChange` _(optional)_ | `(index) => void`                      | Called when the active item changes. |

**Returns:** `activeIndex` (or `-1` if all are disabled), `setActiveIndex`, `getItemProps(index)`.

## Execution flow

1. Render: if the stored index is out of range or disabled, the first enabled item becomes active (derived, no effect).
2. Keydown on an item: compute the next enabled index, `preventDefault()`, set it active and focus its element (refs registered by `getItemProps`).
3. Modified keys (Alt/Ctrl/Meta) are left alone so browser and screen-reader shortcuts keep working.

## Common mistakes

### Every item in the Tab order

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
buttons.map((b) => <button tabIndex={0}>…</button>);
```

Keyboard users must Tab through every item; APG composite widgets are one Tab stop.

### Forgetting the semantics

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
<div>
  {items.map((item, i) => (
    <button {...getItemProps(i)} />
  ))}
</div>
```

The hook manages focus only. Add `role="toolbar"`/`"tablist"` with a label, `aria-orientation` for vertical tab lists, and `aria-pressed`/`aria-selected` as appropriate.

## Edge cases

- APG suggests keeping disabled toolbar items focusable (with `aria-disabled`) so they are discoverable — then do not report them via `isDisabled`.
- Text inputs inside a roving group need Left/Right for the caret; avoid them in horizontal groups.
- When an action disables the focused item, move focus first (the toolbar demo’s "Clear formatting").

User-event tests cover the single Tab stop and remembered position, arrows, Home/End, wrapping vs `loop: false`, vertical orientation, RTL, skipping disabled items, ignored modifier keys, click-to-activate and fallback when the active item disappears.
